bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body: Sustained Middle East conflict driving fuel costs; Delay in Nagaur due to Supreme Court Aravalli ruling; Pricing power inability to pass through INR400/ton cost hike; Clinker availability constraint (93% util) mitigated by blended ratio improvement (62% -> 65%+).
bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body: Cautiously optimistic on volume (>industry growth) but transparent on margin compression; Confident on long-term 30MT goal despite Assam mining setback; Defensive on cost mitigation levers.
bull_bear.title: Management quality / tone

bull_bear.body: Derecognition of INR325cr intangible assets (mining rights) due to AMDCL contract cancellation in Assam, yet management confirms viability of NE plant via 2 alternative auctioned mines (250MT reserves); RMC growth deliberately curbed to focus on higher-margin non-cement products like adhesives.
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

business.body: Cement volume driven by housing/infra; Non-cement (INR169cr) includes high-margin adhesives/tile solutions; RMC (INR82cr) growth deliberately slowed to protect margins; AAC blocks (INR59cr) on plan.

business.body:
- [Promoter structure] The Company states it has only one Promoter, namely Bengal & Assam Company Limited, and that Dwarkesh Energy Limited is a Promoter Group entity and not a Promoter as IiAS had reported; Smt. Vinita Singhania is described as a constituent of the Promoter Group and not the Promoter.
- [AGM / Governance] IiAS recommended AGAINST Item 5 of the AGM Notice — re-appointment of Smt. Vinita Singhania as Chairperson & Managing Director for five years from 01 August 2026 with remuneration fixed as minimum remuneration — citing (G) Governance Concern and (T) Weak Transparency; the Company asked IiAS to change the recommendation from AGAINST to FOR and issue an Addendum.
- [Remuneration framework] The Company states the total remuneration (Fixed and Variable) of Smt. Vinita Singhania together with the Dy. Managing Director (Shri Shrivats Singhania) and President & Director (Dr. Arun Kumar Shukla) shall be within the permitted limit of 10% of Net Profit for all managerial personnel under Section 197 of the Companies Act, 2013, with minimum remuneration and no commission in the event of loss or inadequate profits under Section IV of Part II of Schedule V.
- [Variable pay] The Company declines to quantify a cap: it states that since it is difficult to project future profits, neither the Commission nor an absolute cap on variable pay can be quantified at this stage, and that the Performance Linked Incentive is only an enabling approval as the Company presently does not have any PLI Scheme.
- [NRC process] The Company states Smt. Vinita Singhania abstained when her remuneration and re-appointment were discussed in the Nomination & Remuneration Committee (chaired by an Independent Director) and that the matter was approved by all the Independent Directors forming part of the NRC, hence no conflict of interest.

deepdive.thesis: JK Lakshmi navigates a severe Q4 cost shock (petcoke +40% QoQ) with limited pricing power, compressing EBITDA/ton to ~INR730, while aggressively pursuing a INR5,500+ crore capex plan to reach 30MT by 2030 despite the derecognition of INR325 crore intangible assets from the cancelled Assam mining contract.

open.item: Capacity expansion programme toward 30 million tonnes of cement capacity by 2030 remains on track.
Mission to achieve a turnover of INR 30,000 Crores by 2030.
Targeting to be 7 times water positive by FY 2029-30 (currently 4.49 times water positive).
Target of 100% renewable power share in total electrical power consumption by 2040 (currently ~47%).
Adopted a science-based approach through an SBTi commitment, with near-term emissions-reduction targets under validation process.
Vision to be among the top three companies in the industry in terms of EBIDTA per ton margins.
Mission to develop innovative solutions, expand asset footprint, and venture into new business opportunities contributing 40% of the business.
Contracts remaining to be executed on capital account (net of advances) stood at INR 1,015.45 crore as at 31 March 2026, representing contracted capex yet to be incurred.
Expansion of limestone production capacity at the Durg (Chhattisgarh) Mine Lease II from 0.3 Million TPA to 1.35 Million TPA, under EIA process.
Expansion in production capacity of the captive limestone mines (Mine Lease I, Durg, Chhattisgarh) from 4.8 MTPA to 8 MTPA, with additional crushing capacity of 1,500 TPH, under EIA process.
Proposed standalone Cement Grinding Project of 3.0 Million TPA at Lohat, Block Pandaul, District Madhubani, Bihar, for OPC, PSC, PPC and Composite Cement.
Proposed new limestone mine 'Mudhvay Sub Block A' (Area 198.90.98 ha) with limestone production capacity of 2.5 Million TPA at Kachchh, Gujarat, under EIA process.

risks.note: The Company flags this as the 'central risk': input costs (especially fuel and packaging) are expected to keep rising in FY2026-27, mirroring the FY2022-23 scenario where cost increases outpaced price hikes; estimated cost rise of ₹300-400/tonne for FY2026-27 with price hikes likely to lag, widening the gap between cost inflation and realisation growth.
risks.risk: Margin sustainability — cost inflation outpacing price realisation

risks.note: Industry capacity utilisation is projected to stay around ~70% even on an expanded base in FY2026-27; over 60 million MTPA of capacity was added industry-wide in FY2025-26 alone, with North India capacity growing at a 12% CAGR through FY2027-28, heightening regional price volatility and keeping sector pricing CAGR estimated in negative territory (1-2%) since FY2022-23.

The Strait of Hormuz carries ~20% of global oil/LNG trade; Indian cement makers source ~50% of pet coke from Saudi Arabia and the UAE. Even a negotiated reopening offers limited relief, as war-risk insurance premiums (previously ~0.25% of hull value) could rise materially, keeping freight and insurance costs structurally elevated for years.
risks.risk: Hormuz Strait closure — structural fuel/logistics chokepoint

risks.note: Imported petcoke and coal prices have risen ~40% and ~35% respectively since the West Asia conflict began, to an estimated $160-170/MT; with fuel and power at 30-35% of production costs, this translates to roughly ₹300/MT of unbudgeted cost pressure, and refiners shifting toward gas production could further constrain pet coke availability — a supply issue, not just a pricing one.

Shipping lines have imposed war-risk surcharges of $1,500-2,000 per container on Gulf cargo, rerouting via the Cape of Good Hope adds 10-14 days per voyage, and the Rupee's breach of 95/USD amplifies every dollar-denominated import (pet coke, gypsum, freight), compounding cost pressure from both commodity and currency risk simultaneously.

The cost of polypropylene bags used for cement packaging has nearly doubled, adding an estimated ₹60-80 per tonne, compounded by the Middle East conflict; the full effect is expected to hit margins from Q1 FY2026-27 onward, coinciding with peak fuel costs.

Infrastructure-led demand is the industry's core demand thesis, but execution risk is real: government capex declined 24% year-on-year in January 2026, and PMAY-Rural/PMGSY targets were missed in both FY2024-25 and FY2025-26; continued macro stress (conflict, inflation, fiscal compression, RBI policy constraints) could further erode the demand cushion via capex deferral and softness in private housing.
risks.risk: Government capex slippage and infrastructure-demand execution risk
